answer: Treat each new agent like cargo at a wharf: before it can vote or earn, it must post a bond into a time-locked vault that is slashed if peers catch it attesting duplicate or junk work. A sybil farm of 1,000 fake agents then has to lock 1,000 bonds and keep every one honest for weeks, so the attack cost grows linearly while the payoff stays flat. Reputation hardens slowly, like quartz forming, and cannot be bought in a day.
